# Tricks reference

<!-- This page is generated by `bun scripts/tricks-reference.ts --write` from web/src/lib/tricks/catalogue.ts. Do not edit it by hand. -->

This page lists every place, part, manifest key, limit and command of a ColliePWA trick, and it is complete. It is generated from the code, so it cannot drift. It is the one list: other pages link here and do not repeat its tables.

## Places

A place is a spot on the phone where a trick can show (a surface). A program trick, a program on your machine that prints parts, draws in the first five. An agent view, one screen that the session's own agent draws, is the sixth.

| Place | Name | Where it shows | Drawn by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `belt` | Belt | A mark at the end of the Belt, the scrolling strip of controls. It never takes fixed room. | A program |
| `session` | Page | A page of the trick's own: a row on the Dashboard under Tricks, and a screen of its own. The code word is `session`. | A program |
| `dashboard` | Dashboard tile | A round tile in the strip at the top of the Dashboard. The strip is hidden while no trick has a tile. | A program |
| `status` | Status chip | One chip in the status line above the Belt, after Collie's own items. | A program |
| `tabbar` | Bottom bar item | An item in the Dashboard's bottom bar, after the Hill. | A program |
| `agent-view` | Agent view | A view of one agent session, beside Terminal and Chat. The session's own agent draws it, and the person switches it on per session. | A session's agent |

### `belt`

**Where.** A mark at the end of the Belt, the scrolling strip of controls. It never takes fixed room.

**Shows.** One mark: an icon, a face word (`label`), a `badge` and a `tone`. It takes no view.

**A tap.** With an `intent`, a tap runs the trick with that intent. Without one, the mark is the same button and takes no tap.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Parts of this place per trick | one |
| `label`, the face word | at most 12 characters |
| `badge` | a count from 0 to 9999 as text, or "" for a dot |
| A mark needs | at least one of `icon`, `label` and `badge` |
| One part, as compact JSON | at most 16 KiB |

A program prints:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "parts": [
    {
      "at": "belt",
      "id": "legs",
      "mark": {
        "icon": "check",
        "label": "23/34",
        "tone": "ok",
        "intent": "open"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `session`

**Where.** A page of the trick's own: a row on the Dashboard under Tricks, and a screen of its own. The code word is `session`.

**Shows.** A name, an icon, a tone, a subtitle, a badge, a progress meter, up to four action buttons and a `view`: a list of nodes of any kind in the Parts table.

**A tap.** A button, or an action, sends its intent to the trick, which runs once with that tap. A `row` or a `link` with an `href` opens a web page or a session.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | at most 40 characters. Left out, the manifest's name |
| `subtitle` | at most 120 characters |
| `badge` | `{ "count": 0 to 9999 }` or `{ "text": 1 to 12 characters }`, one of the two |
| `progress` | `value` of `max`, `max` a whole number from 1 to 12. No `value` means indeterminate |
| `actions` | at most 4, each `id`, `label` (at most 16 characters), `intent`, and optionally `value`, `icon` and `disabled`. An action icon is one of `play`, `pause`, `check`, `x`, `refresh`, `archive`, `flag`, `star`, `send`, `note`, `search`, `more` |
| `view` | 1 to 24 nodes at the top, 6 levels, 300 nodes in all |
| Parts of this place per trick | as many as it needs, each with its own `id` |
| One part, as compact JSON | at most 16 KiB |

A program prints:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "parts": [
    {
      "at": "session",
      "id": "main",
      "name": "Legs",
      "icon": "check",
      "subtitle": "3 of 5 done",
      "badge": {
        "count": 2
      },
      "progress": {
        "value": 3,
        "max": 5
      },
      "actions": [
        {
          "id": "refresh",
          "label": "Refresh",
          "intent": "refresh",
          "icon": "refresh"
        }
      ],
      "view": [
        {
          "kind": "list",
          "kids": [
            {
              "kind": "row",
              "text": "api",
              "attrs": {
                "end": "ok",
                "tone": "ok"
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### `dashboard`

**Where.** A round tile in the strip at the top of the Dashboard. The strip is hidden while no trick has a tile.

**Shows.** One item: an icon over a short name, with a `badge` and a `tone`. It takes no view.

**A tap.** A tap opens the trick's Page when it has one. Without a Page the tile is drawn and takes no tap.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Parts of this place per trick | one |
| `label` | 1 to 16 characters |
| `badge` | a count from 0 to 9999 (0 draws none), or text of 1 to 12 characters |
| One part, as compact JSON | at most 16 KiB |

A program prints:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "parts": [
    {
      "at": "dashboard",
      "id": "legs",
      "item": {
        "label": "Legs",
        "icon": "check",
        "badge": 3,
        "tone": "ok"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `status`

**Where.** One chip in the status line above the Belt, after Collie's own items.

**Shows.** One chip: a short text, an icon, a `tone`, and a live time with `at` and `clock`. It takes no view.

**A tap.** A tap opens the trick's Page when it has one. The chip is not a control and takes no intent.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Parts of this place per trick | one |
| `text` | 1 to 12 characters |
| One part, as compact JSON | at most 16 KiB |

A program prints:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "parts": [
    {
      "at": "status",
      "id": "ci",
      "chip": {
        "text": "CI green",
        "icon": "check",
        "tone": "ok"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `tabbar`

**Where.** An item in the Dashboard's bottom bar, after the Hill.

**Shows.** One item: an icon over a short name, with a `badge` and a `tone`. It takes no view.

**A tap.** A tap opens the trick's Page when it has one. Without a Page the item is drawn and takes no tap.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Parts of this place per trick | one |
| `label` | 1 to 16 characters |
| `badge` | a count from 0 to 9999 (0 draws none), or text of 1 to 12 characters |
| One part, as compact JSON | at most 16 KiB |

A program prints:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "parts": [
    {
      "at": "tabbar",
      "id": "legs",
      "item": {
        "label": "Legs",
        "icon": "check",
        "badge": "new"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `agent-view`

**Where.** A view of one agent session, beside Terminal and Chat. The session's own agent draws it, and the person switches it on per session.

**Shows.** One screen: a list of nodes in the Parts table's kinds (held tighter, see Parts), up to four pictures, and one decision block with a question and up to five options.

**A tap.** A tap on a button, or a pick in the decision block, sends a message in the person's name to that one session. It carries the label only: a button holds no hidden value. Collie marks the pick on the screen afterwards. The agent cannot: a button's `pressed` and a choice's `picked` are refused.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Contract | 2, and the manifest needs `rules` |
| Screen title | at most 80 characters |
| The note of `start` | at most 80 characters |
| A button's label | one line, at most 60 characters |
| A group's label | one line, at most 40 characters |
| The view, as compact JSON | at most 16 KiB, and the view limits of a part |
| Pictures | at most 4 on a screen, 2 MiB each, 8 MiB together, caption at most 80 characters |
| Decision block | a question of at most 120 characters, 1 to 5 options |
| A pending block's label | at most 40 characters |
| Writes by the agent | 120 a minute for one trick and session |
| Sends from the view | 20 a minute for one session, one in flight at a time |
| Marks of a pick | Collie's, never the agent's. A redraw keeps a mark while a block of the same id holds a button at the same steps, and the decision block's while it asks the same question with the same options |
| Links | a web address only. A session `href` is refused. The phone shows the host after each link, whole |
| Collie's own words | no text of the agent's may say "From Collie", "Drawn by this session's agent", "Drawn in an earlier conversation", "Sent to this session", "A question waits in this session", "Your typing answers the question", "The screen changed", "The buttons wait", "The agent is working", "Tap again to send", "Earlier screen", "The agent answered in text". A text is read as whole words, in any case, with look-alike letters and hidden characters folded. Collie's bare name passes |
| The rules file | see Limits: the rules file |

In `trick.toml`:

```toml
id = "triage"
name = "Triage"
contract = 2
places = ["agent-view"]
rules = "rules.md"
```

The agent passes `show` this file:

```json
[
  {
    "kind": "card",
    "attrs": {
      "tone": "accent"
    },
    "kids": [
      {
        "kind": "para",
        "text": "Two tests fail."
      },
      {
        "kind": "button",
        "attrs": {
          "label": "Show me the first one",
          "intent": "show-first"
        }
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## The Hill

A page of Decisions: questions that a program or an agent asks the person, each answered with one tap. It is built in. A trick does not list it in `places`. Settings → Tricks shows it as the first row, tagged "Built in", with its one switch.

**From a program.** A program lists Decisions in the `decisions` key of its output (the helper's `t.decide`). The list is declarative: after each run that succeeded, Collie makes the Hill agree with it, as [The list is the truth](#the-list-is-the-truth) says below. A document lists at most 20.

**From an agent.** An agent posts one with `collie hill post` and reads the answer with `collie hill status <id>`. The answer also reaches the agent as a WalkyTalky message.

A Decision a program lists has these keys:

| Key | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | text | yes | 1 to 64 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, unique in the document | The trick's own name for the Decision. The answer comes back with it. |
| `title` | text | yes | at most 120 characters | The question, as a sentence the options answer. |
| `summary` | text | yes | at most 280 characters | What the recommended option does, and the one fact that decides it. |
| `body` | text | no | at most 4000 characters | Longer text, shown behind More. |
| `options` | list | no | at most 5; each `intent`, `label` (at most 40), and optionally `detail` (at most 120) and `confirm` (at most 24) | The choices. A tap on one sends its `intent` back. |
| `recommends` | object or null | no | `{ intent, why }`, `why` at most 200 characters | The trick's pick, one of the options. Shown as Recommended, never pre-selected. |
| `priority` | word | no | one of `now`, `today`, `later`. Default `today` | A request, not a fact. Only `now` sends a notification, and one sender holds at most 3 open `now` Decisions. |
| `text` | word | no | one of `none`, `optional`, `required`. Default `optional` | Whether the person may, must, or may not add words to the answer. `none` needs at least one option. |
| `about` | session id | no | an `id` from the facts' sessions, `memberId:paneId` | The session the card is about. The card opens its Chat. |
| `replyTo` | session id | no | an `id` from the facts' sessions | The session that gets the person's words, as the person's own WalkyTalky message. |
| `media` | list | no | at most 4; each `file` (a PNG, JPEG or WebP in the trick's folder, 2 MiB at most) and optionally `caption` (at most 80 characters) | Pictures on the card. |
| `links` | list | no | at most 5; each `label` (at most 40) and `href` (an https or http address, at most 500 characters) | Web pages that give more. |
| `expiresAt` | instant | no | epoch milliseconds. Left out, 14 days; never more than 30 days | When the Decision closes by itself, as expired. |
| `view` | list of nodes | no | see Parts: a Decision's view | A small display-only view under the summary: facts to read, never a control. |

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Open Decisions per sender | 20 |
| Open `now` Decisions per sender | 3. A further one shows as `today` |
| Closed Decisions served | 20, newest first |
| The person's words in an answer | at most 4000 characters |
| Expiry | 14 days when left out, at most 30 |
| Answers waiting for one trick | 32. One more is refused as busy |

**The answer.** When the person answers, the program runs once with a `tap` trigger. Its `node` is `hill/<key>`. Its `intent` is the chosen option's, `answer` for words alone, or `dismiss`. Its `value` is `{ "text": ... }`, the person's words or `null`. Its `seen` is the hash of the version the person saw, so the trick can tell an answer to old words from one to new.

A program lists this Decision:

```json
{
  "key": "case-24",
  "title": "Rerun the failed check?",
  "summary": "Check 24 failed twice, on a timeout. A rerun takes about a minute.",
  "options": [
    {
      "intent": "rerun",
      "label": "Rerun it"
    },
    {
      "intent": "skip",
      "label": "Skip it"
    }
  ],
  "recommends": {
    "intent": "rerun",
    "why": "It failed on a timeout, not on a test."
  }
}
```

The answer comes back as this trigger:

```json
{
  "kind": "tap",
  "rid": "0b9e8d7c-3a41-4c52-9d5e-1f2a3b4c5d6e",
  "node": "hill/case-24",
  "intent": "rerun",
  "value": {
    "text": "Rerun it, then tell me."
  },
  "seen": "944a71314b332828"
}
```

From a terminal:

```sh
collie hill post --title "Rerun the failed check?" --summary "Check 24 failed on a timeout." --option rerun="Rerun it" --option skip="Skip it" --recommend rerun --why "It was a timeout."
```

### The list is the truth

After each run that succeeded, Collie makes the Hill agree with the list of `decisions`, key by key.

| When | Collie does |
| --- | --- |
| A new `key` | Posts once. A second run, or a restart, posts nothing twice. |
| A listed `key` with changed content | Posts the new version, which replaces the open one. Content is the title, summary, body, options, recommendation, text mode, links, priority, `about`, `replyTo`, the view, and each picture's bytes and caption. When the old card is closed, the new version posts as a fresh card. |
| A `key` the list no longer holds | The card is withdrawn, "by the trick". |
| A `key` the person answered or dismissed | Stays closed while its content is unchanged. To ask again, change the content, or drop the key for one run and list it again. |
| A `key` that closed without the person: `undeliverable`, `expired` or `withdrawn`, a withdrawal by anyone but the trick | Posts again on a later run that still lists it, at most once every 10 minutes for that key. A new post of this kind never sends a notification. |
| A document with no `decisions` key | Changes nothing. |
| `decisions` is `[]` | Withdraws every open card of the trick. |
| A Decision the parser or the Hill refuses, or that names a session that is not there | Changes nothing for its key: the version on the Hill stays. It shows as a refusal. |
| A failed or timed-out run | Changes nothing. |
| The trick switched off or removed | Every open card of the trick is withdrawn at once, "the trick is off". |
| The Hill switched off | No post, replace or withdraw happens, and the trick still runs. Its row says its Decisions are not shown. |

So list every Decision you still want on every run, and keep the words stable. Words that change on each run, such as an age in minutes, post a new version every time and ask again.

### Wording a card

A person opens the card cold, between other things, so the words carry the decision.

| Part | How to write it |
| --- | --- |
| Title | The decision as a short question that the options answer, at most 60 characters. "Ship 1.28.1 to Stable now?" is good. "Are the new kinds right?" is not. |
| Summary | At most 2 sentences and 200 characters. The first says what the recommended option does. The second gives the one fact that decides it. The evidence goes in the view or the body. |
| Option | Starts with a verb and says what happens, such as "Hold until CI". Never a bare Yes or No. |

`collie trick dev` and `collie trick check --run` warn about a title past 60 characters or with no question mark, a summary past 2 sentences or 200 characters, and an option that says only Yes, No or OK. A warning never refuses.

## Parts

A part, in this page, is one node of a view: the building block a view is made of (the schema calls it a node kind). A node is `{ "kind": ..., "text"?: ..., "attrs"?: ..., "kids"?: ... }`, and every attribute value is text.

- A program's view, on its Page (a `session` part): every kind.
- A Decision's view, under its summary: display only. It takes `group`, `list`, `row`, `bar`, `chip`, `para`, `line`, `run`, `code`, `link`, `meter`, `spacer`, `number`, `image`, `compare`, `table`, `col`, `cell`, `diff` or `spark`. At most 8 KiB, 100 nodes and 4 levels.
- An agent view: every kind, read strictly. A kind or an attribute that a program's part would only leave out is refused.

| Part | What it is | Sits | In a Decision's view |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `card` | A block that groups what belongs together. Its `tone` colours its edge. | the top of a view | no |
| `group` | A titled set of rows and other nodes. The person can fold it. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group, in a list | yes |
| `list` | A list of rows and groups. It keeps the height of its kids, so a change inside one row moves nothing. | the top of a view | yes |
| `row` | One line: a title, an optional end word, and optionally a second line, chips and one trailing button. | in a group, in a list | yes |
| `bar` | A strip of buttons, chips and links. With `role` `strip` it scrolls sideways as a band. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group | yes |
| `chip` | A small label. `state` draws a dot, `current` marks the step, and `at` with `clock` makes it a live time. | in a card, in a row, in a bar | yes |
| `button` | Sends one intent to the trick on a tap, or copies a text with `does` set to `copy`. | in a card, in a row, in a bar | no |
| `para` | One paragraph of plain text, or of `run` and `link` kids. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group, in a row | yes |
| `line` | One line of monospace screen text, such as a command or a log line. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group, in a code | yes |
| `run` | A piece of text inside a `para` or a `line`, with its own style, link or live time. | in a para, in a line | yes |
| `code` | A block of code. Its kids are `line` nodes. It scrolls on its own past `max` lines. | the top of a view | yes |
| `link` | A link that opens a web page, or one agent session of the crew. | in a group, in a bar, in a para, in a line | yes |
| `image` | A picture. In a program's part it is a file of the trick's `media/` folder. In a Decision's view or an agent view it names one of the pictures that came with it, by `ref`. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group, in a compare | yes |
| `meter` | An amount, or the progress of a task. With `role` `progress` and no `value` it is indeterminate. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group | yes |
| `spacer` | Space between nodes. With a `label` it is a divider with words. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group | yes |
| `number` | A big figure with a label under it. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group | yes |
| `compare` | Two images side by side at one height, as before and after. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group | yes |
| `table` | A small table: its column heads first, then its cells row by row. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group | yes |
| `col` | A column head of a `table`. It sits only inside a `table`. | in a table | yes |
| `cell` | One cell of a `table`. It sits only inside a `table`. An empty cell has no `text`. | in a table | yes |
| `diff` | A hunk of a diff. Each line starts with `+` (added), `-` (removed) or `@@` (a hunk head). | the top of a view, in a card, in a group | yes |
| `spark` | A trend as a small line with no axes. The last point is marked. | the top of a view, in a card, in a group | yes |

### `card`

A block that groups what belongs together. Its `tone` colours its edge.

**Sits.** the top of a view.

**Holds.** `para`, `line`, `chip`, `button`, `meter`, `image`, `bar`, `group`, `number`, `spacer`, `compare`, `table`, `diff` or `spark` (1 to 24).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | tone | no | one of `plain`, `accent`, `warn`, `danger`, `ok`, `muted` | The colour of the card's edge. |

```json
{
  "kind": "card",
  "attrs": {
    "tone": "ok"
  },
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "para",
      "text": "All checks passed."
    }
  ]
}
```

### `group`

A titled set of rows and other nodes. The person can fold it.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group, in a list.

**Holds.** `row`, `group`, `bar`, `para`, `line`, `link`, `meter`, `number`, `spacer`, `image`, `compare`, `table`, `diff` or `spark` (1 to 24).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | text | no | at most 60 characters | The group's title. |
| `fold` | word | no | one of `open`, `closed` | Whether the group starts open or closed. The person owns the toggle after the first draw. |
| `badge` | count or dot | no | a count from 0 to 9999 as text, or "" for a dot | A count, or a dot, beside the title. |

**In an agent view.** A `label` is one line of at most 40 characters, because a tap inside the group sends it.

```json
{
  "kind": "group",
  "attrs": {
    "label": "Services",
    "fold": "open"
  },
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "row",
      "text": "api",
      "attrs": {
        "end": "ok"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `list`

A list of rows and groups. It keeps the height of its kids, so a change inside one row moves nothing.

**Sits.** the top of a view.

**Holds.** `group` or `row` (0 to 50).

```json
{
  "kind": "list",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "row",
      "text": "api"
    },
    {
      "kind": "row",
      "text": "web"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `row`

One line: a title, an optional end word, and optionally a second line, chips and one trailing button.

**Sits.** in a group, in a list.

**Holds.** `para`, `chip` or `button` (0 to 24).

**Text.** The row's title. (required, at most 120 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | address | no | with no `rel`, an https or http address (at most 2048 characters) or a session's `id` from the facts | Makes the row tappable: an https or http address, or a session's `id` from the facts. |
| `end` | text | no | at most 24 characters | A short word at the end of the row. |
| `badge` | count or dot | no | a count from 0 to 9999 as text, or "" for a dot | A count, or a dot, on the row. |
| `tone` | tone | no | one of `plain`, `accent`, `warn`, `danger`, `ok`, `muted` | The tone of the row. |
| `cut` | word | no | one of `end`, `mid` | Where a long title is cut. |
| `icon` | icon | no | one of the icon words in Shared values | An icon at the start of the row. |
| `disabled` | text | no | at most 120 characters, may be empty | The reason the row cannot be used. An empty text means no reason is given. |

**In an agent view.** An `href` is a web address only: a session is refused.

**In a Decision's view.** A row opens a web page at most. It takes no button.

```json
{
  "kind": "list",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "row",
      "text": "api",
      "attrs": {
        "end": "ok",
        "tone": "ok",
        "icon": "check"
      },
      "kids": [
        {
          "kind": "para",
          "text": "Deployed 2 min ago"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### `bar`

A strip of buttons, chips and links. With `role` `strip` it scrolls sideways as a band.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group.

**Holds.** `button`, `chip` or `link` (1 to 12).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `role` | word | no | one of `strip` | `strip` makes the bar one band that scrolls sideways. |
| `scroll` | word | no | one of `x` | Sideways scroll for a bar of chips. |
| `label` | text | no | at most 40 characters | A short name for the bar. |

```json
{
  "kind": "bar",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "button",
      "attrs": {
        "label": "Rerun",
        "intent": "rerun"
      }
    },
    {
      "kind": "chip",
      "text": "3 failed",
      "attrs": {
        "tone": "danger"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `chip`

A small label. `state` draws a dot, `current` marks the step, and `at` with `clock` makes it a live time.

**Sits.** in a card, in a row, in a bar.

**Text.** The words of the chip. They may be left out when the chip is a live time (`at` and `clock`). (optional, at most 60 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | tone | no | one of `plain`, `accent`, `warn`, `danger`, `ok`, `muted` | The tone of the chip. |
| `icon` | icon | no | one of the icon words in Shared values | An icon before the text. |
| `at` | instant | no | epoch milliseconds as digits, such as `"1794130692000"` | An instant that the chip shows as a live time. It goes with `clock`. |
| `clock` | word | no | one of `ago`, `elapsed`, `left`, `time` | How the instant is told. It goes with `at`. |
| `state` | word | no | one of `working`, `waiting`, `idle`, `done`, `gone` | Draws a status dot. Chips with a `state` in a `bar` draw a strip of steps. |
| `current` | flag | no | the empty text `""` when on, left out when off | Marks this chip as the current step. |
| `short` | text | no | at most 12 characters | The text shown when the box is narrow. |

```json
{
  "kind": "card",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "chip",
      "text": "building",
      "attrs": {
        "state": "working",
        "icon": "refresh"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `button`

Sends one intent to the trick on a tap, or copies a text with `does` set to `copy`.

**Sits.** in a card, in a row, in a bar.

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `intent` | intent | yes, unless `does` is `copy` | 1 to 48 of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit | The intent a tap sends to the trick. |
| `label` | text | yes | at most 24 characters | The words on the button. |
| `tone` | tone | no | one of `plain`, `accent`, `warn`, `danger`, `ok`, `muted` | The tone of the button. |
| `disabled` | text | no | at most 120 characters, may be empty | The reason the button cannot be used. An empty text means no reason is given. |
| `pressed` | word | no | one of `true`, `false`, `mixed` | Draws the button as a toggle: on, off or mixed. An agent view refuses it: Collie marks the pick. |
| `confirm` | text | no | at most 24 characters | A second label. The first tap arms the button and the second sends the intent. |
| `badge` | count or dot | no | a count from 0 to 9999 as text, or "" for a dot | A count, or a dot, on the button. |
| `icon` | icon | no | one of the icon words in Shared values | An icon on the button. |
| `hint` | text | no | at most 120 characters | A short line of help for the button. |
| `does` | word | no | one of `copy` | `copy` copies `value` to the phone's clipboard instead of sending an intent. |
| `value` | text | yes, when `does` is `copy` | 1 to 1024 bytes, no control or invisible character | The one fixed text a tap sends with the intent, or the text `copy` copies. |

**In an agent view.** A tap sends the label (and the label of the group it sits in). `value`, `does` and `pressed` are refused: Collie marks the pick, the agent does not. The label is one line of at most 60 characters, and says none of Collie's own words.

```json
{
  "kind": "card",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "button",
      "attrs": {
        "label": "Rerun",
        "intent": "rerun",
        "tone": "accent"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `para`

One paragraph of plain text, or of `run` and `link` kids.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group, in a row.

**Holds.** `run` or `link` (1 to 64).

**Text.** The paragraph's words. Give `text`, or `run` and `link` kids, exactly one of the two. (optional, at most 2000 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `role` | word | no | one of `heading`, `quote` | Draws the paragraph as a heading or a quote. |
| `bullet` | text | no | at most 4 characters | A marker before the paragraph, such as `-` or `1.`. |
| `term` | text | no | at most 40 characters | A short term that the paragraph defines. |

```json
{
  "kind": "para",
  "text": "Three checks failed on the last run."
}
```

### `line`

One line of monospace screen text, such as a command or a log line.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group, in a code.

**Holds.** `run` or `link` (1 to 64).

**Text.** The line's words, a tab allowed. Give `text`, or `run` and `link` kids, never both. (optional, at most 240 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | style words | no | words with single spaces between, each once, from Shared values | Style words for the whole line. |
| `role` | word | no | one of `text`, `status`, `note` | Draws the line as plain text, a status line or a note. |

```json
{
  "kind": "line",
  "text": "$ bun test",
  "attrs": {
    "style": "dim"
  }
}
```

### `run`

A piece of text inside a `para` or a `line`, with its own style, link or live time.

**Sits.** in a para, in a line.

**Text.** The piece of text. Spaces alone are allowed. (required, at most 2000 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | style words | no | words with single spaces between, each once, from Shared values | Style words for this piece of text. |
| `code` | flag | no | the empty text `""` when on, left out when off | A flag: draws the text as inline code. |
| `href` | web address | no | https or http, at most 2048 characters | Makes the text a link to a web address. |
| `at` | instant | no | epoch milliseconds as digits, such as `"1794130692000"` | An instant that the text shows as a live time. It goes with `clock`. |
| `clock` | word | no | one of `ago`, `elapsed`, `left`, `time` | How the instant is told. It goes with `at`. |

**In an agent view.** Text with an `href` that reads as a web address must be that address. The `href` is a web address only, and the phone shows its host after the run.

```json
{
  "kind": "para",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "run",
      "text": "Build "
    },
    {
      "kind": "run",
      "text": "passed",
      "attrs": {
        "style": "bold"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `code`

A block of code. Its kids are `line` nodes. It scrolls on its own past `max` lines.

**Sits.** the top of a view.

**Holds.** `line` (1 to 200).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lang` | word | no | 1 to 24 of `a-z`, `0-9`, `+`, `#`, `.`, `_` and `-` | The language word of the code. |
| `max` | whole number | no | 1 to 40, as text | How many lines show before the block scrolls on its own. |

```json
{
  "kind": "code",
  "attrs": {
    "lang": "ts"
  },
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "line",
      "text": "const total = 3;"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `link`

A link that opens a web page, or one agent session of the crew.

**Sits.** in a group, in a bar, in a para, in a line.

**Text.** The words of the link. (required, at most 120 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `href` | address | yes | with no `rel`, an https or http address (at most 2048 characters) or a session's `id` from the facts | Where the link goes: a web address, or a session's `id` from the facts with `rel` `pane`. |
| `rel` | word | no | one of `url`, `file`, `pane` | What the `href` names: `url` or `pane`. `file` is refused: a trick opens no file. |
| `badge` | count or dot | no | a count from 0 to 9999 as text, or "" for a dot | A count, or a dot, on the link. |
| `icon` | icon | no | one of the icon words in Shared values | An icon before the link text. |

**In an agent view.** Text that reads as a web address must be that address, in any script. The `href` is a web address only: a session is refused. The phone shows the host after the link.

**In a Decision's view.** A link opens a web page only.

```json
{
  "kind": "group",
  "attrs": {
    "label": "More"
  },
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "link",
      "text": "Open the run",
      "attrs": {
        "href": "https://example.com/run/1"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `image`

A picture. In a program's part it is a file of the trick's `media/` folder. In a Decision's view or an agent view it names one of the pictures that came with it, by `ref`.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group, in a compare.

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | picture path | in a program's part | a `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.webp` file in `media/`, such as `media/chart.png`, with no step that starts with a dot | A picture file in the trick's `media/` folder. Used in a program's part. |
| `alt` | text | in a program's part | at most 120 characters, may be empty | What the picture shows, in words. |
| `w` | whole number | in a program's part | 1 to 4096, as text | The picture's width in pixels. It reserves the box. |
| `h` | whole number | in a program's part | 1 to 4096, as text | The picture's height in pixels. It reserves the box. |
| `ref` | whole number | in a Decision's view and an agent view | 0 to 3, as text | The place of one of the Decision's or the screen's own pictures, counted from 0. Used in a Decision's view and an agent view. |
| `caption` | text | no | at most 80 characters | A line of words under the picture. In a `compare` it labels the frame. |
| `fit` | word | no | one of `contain`, `cover` | `contain` shows the whole picture. `cover` fills the frame and cuts the edges. |
| `focus` | numbers | no | `"x y"` or `"x y zoom"`: x and y from 0 to 100 (percent), zoom from 1 to 8 | The point of the picture to keep in the middle of its frame, and how far to zoom in on it. |

**In an agent view.** The agent adds pictures with `--image` (at most 4) and names each by `ref`.

**In a Decision's view.** Names one of the Decision's own pictures by `ref`.

```json
{
  "kind": "image",
  "attrs": {
    "src": "media/chart.png",
    "alt": "Latency chart",
    "w": "640",
    "h": "360"
  }
}
```

### `meter`

An amount, or the progress of a task. With `role` `progress` and no `value` it is indeterminate.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group.

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | yes, unless `role` is `progress` | 0 or more, as text, such as `"68"` or `"0.5"` | How much, from 0 to `max`. |
| `max` | number | no | 0 or more, as text, such as `"68"` or `"0.5"` | The full amount. It defaults to 1. |
| `tone` | tone | no | one of `plain`, `accent`, `warn`, `danger`, `ok`, `muted` | The tone of the meter. |
| `label` | text | no | at most 40 characters | A short name for the meter. |
| `role` | word | no | one of `progress`, `meter` | `meter` is an amount. `progress` is the steps of a task. |

```json
{
  "kind": "meter",
  "attrs": {
    "value": "68",
    "max": "100",
    "label": "Disk",
    "tone": "warn"
  }
}
```

### `spacer`

Space between nodes. With a `label` it is a divider with words.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group.

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | text | no | at most 40 characters | Words in the divider. |

```json
{
  "kind": "spacer",
  "attrs": {
    "label": "Today"
  }
}
```

### `number`

A big figure with a label under it.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group.

**Text.** The figure, such as `23/34` or `1.2k`. (required, at most 12 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | text | no | at most 40 characters | The words under the figure. |
| `tone` | tone | no | one of `plain`, `accent`, `warn`, `danger`, `ok`, `muted` | The tone of the figure. |
| `unit` | text | no | at most 24 characters | A short unit after the figure. |

```json
{
  "kind": "number",
  "text": "23/34",
  "attrs": {
    "label": "checks passed",
    "tone": "ok"
  }
}
```

### `compare`

Two images side by side at one height, as before and after.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group.

**Holds.** exactly two `image`.

**In an agent view.** Two images named by `ref`.

**In a Decision's view.** Two images named by `ref`.

```json
{
  "kind": "compare",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "image",
      "attrs": {
        "src": "media/before.png",
        "alt": "Before",
        "w": "320",
        "h": "200"
      }
    },
    {
      "kind": "image",
      "attrs": {
        "src": "media/after.png",
        "alt": "After",
        "w": "320",
        "h": "200"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `table`

A small table: its column heads first, then its cells row by row.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group.

**Holds.** `col` (1 to 4), then `cell` row by row, at most 12 rows.

```json
{
  "kind": "table",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "col",
      "text": "Check"
    },
    {
      "kind": "col",
      "text": "Time",
      "attrs": {
        "align": "end"
      }
    },
    {
      "kind": "cell",
      "text": "build"
    },
    {
      "kind": "cell",
      "text": "12 s"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `col`

A column head of a `table`. It sits only inside a `table`.

**Sits.** in a table.

**Text.** The column head. (required, at most 40 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | word | no | one of `start`, `end` | Which side of its column the words keep. A column of figures keeps the end side by default. |

```json
{
  "kind": "table",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "col",
      "text": "Check"
    },
    {
      "kind": "cell",
      "text": "build"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `cell`

One cell of a `table`. It sits only inside a `table`. An empty cell has no `text`.

**Sits.** in a table.

**Text.** The cell's words. It may be empty. (optional, at most 120 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | tone | no | one of `plain`, `accent`, `warn`, `danger`, `ok`, `muted` | The tone of the cell. |

```json
{
  "kind": "table",
  "kids": [
    {
      "kind": "col",
      "text": "Check"
    },
    {
      "kind": "cell",
      "text": "build",
      "attrs": {
        "tone": "ok"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

### `diff`

A hunk of a diff. Each line starts with `+` (added), `-` (removed) or `@@` (a hunk head).

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group.

**Text.** The lines of the hunk, one line break between two lines. (required, at most 8040 characters).

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | text | no | at most 120 characters | The name of the file the hunk is from. |

```json
{
  "kind": "diff",
  "text": "@@ -1 +1 @@\n-const a = 1;\n+const a = 2;",
  "attrs": {
    "file": "app.ts"
  }
}
```

### `spark`

A trend as a small line with no axes. The last point is marked.

**Sits.** the top of a view, in a card, in a group.

| Attribute | Type | Needed | Limit | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | numbers | yes | 2 to 32 numbers with one space between | The numbers of the trend, oldest first. |
| `tone` | tone | no | one of `plain`, `accent`, `warn`, `danger`, `ok`, `muted` | The tone of the line. |
| `label` | text | no | at most 40 characters | A short name for the trend. |

```json
{
  "kind": "spark",
  "attrs": {
    "values": "3 5 4 8 6",
    "tone": "accent",
    "label": "latency"
  }
}
```

### Shared values

| Name | Values |
| --- | --- |
| tone | `plain`, `accent`, `warn`, `danger`, `ok`, `muted` |
| icon | `archive`, `back`, `bell`, `branch`, `camera`, `chat`, `check`, `clock`, `close`, `copy`, `crew`, `delete`, `down`, `download`, `edit`, `eye`, `file`, `flag`, `flask`, `folder`, `git-pull-request`, `image`, `info`, `key`, `link`, `lock`, `machine`, `menu`, `mic`, `minus`, `more`, `move`, `next`, `note`, `pause`, `pin`, `play`, `plug`, `plus`, `refresh`, `search`, `send`, `settings`, `share`, `star`, `tag`, `terminal`, `up`, `upload`, `warn`, `x`. The default icon of a trick is `plug` |
| action icon | `play`, `pause`, `check`, `x`, `refresh`, `archive`, `flag`, `star`, `send`, `note`, `search`, `more` |
| chip state | `working`, `waiting`, `idle`, `done`, `gone` |
| clock | `ago`, `elapsed`, `left`, `time` |
| style | `bold`, `dim`, `italic`, `underline`, `inverse`, `strike`, `box`, `fg-<colour>`, `bg-<colour>` and the syntax inks `syn-keyword`, `syn-string`, `syn-comment`, `syn-number`, `syn-type`, `syn-func`, `syn-const`, `syn-punct`. The colours are `black`, `red`, `green`, `yellow`, `blue`, `magenta`, `cyan`, `white`, `bright-black`, `bright-red`, `bright-green`, `bright-yellow`, `bright-blue`, `bright-magenta`, `bright-cyan`, `bright-white` |
| button intent | 1 to 48 of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit |
| Decision option intent | 1 to 32 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, starting with a letter, never `answer` or `dismiss` |

## Manifest keys

These are all the keys of `trick.toml`. At the same contract, any other key is refused, so a typo shows.

| Key | Type | Needed | Limit | Contract | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | text | yes | 1 to 32 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit. It equals the folder's name. Not `walky-talky`, `hill`, `collie`, `view` | 1 | The trick's id, which is also the name of its folder. |
| `name` | text | yes | at most 40 characters | 1 | The name a person reads on the row. |
| `run` | text | yes, unless the trick is only an agent view | at most 1024 characters | 1 | What Collie runs: a TypeScript file in the folder ("program.ts"), or a shell command line. An agent view alone has none. |
| `every` | duration | no | 5s to 24h, one whole number and `s`, `m` or `h`, such as `30s` or `5m` | 1 | How often it runs on its timer. Left out, it runs at start and on taps only. |
| `watch` | list of paths | no | at most 8 paths of at most 1024 characters, each an absolute path, or a path under the home folder written with a leading tilde | 1 | Kept for a later Collie. This one leaves it out with a note. Leave it out. |
| `on` | list of words | no | `session.status`, `turn.end`, `ask.open` | 1 | Kept for a later Collie. This one leaves it out with a note. Leave it out. |
| `mode` | word | no | `once` or `serve`. Default `once` | 1 | `once` runs once per trigger and prints one document. `serve` is kept for a later Collie. |
| `contract` | whole number | no | 1 to 999. Default 1. This Collie speaks 1 to 2 | 1 | The contract the trick is written for. Write 2 to read files with `inputs` or to add an agent view. A higher number than this Collie knows is refused with one line. |
| `icon` | word | no | one of the icon words in Shared values. Default `plug` | 1 | The trick's icon. `collie trick check` names a wrong one. |
| `places` | list of words | yes | 1 to 16 of `belt`, `session`, `dashboard`, `status`, `tabbar`, `agent-view`. Each once | 1 | Where its parts draw. Each place a part uses must be listed. `agent-view` adds an agent view and needs contract 2. |
| `env` | list of names | no | at most 32 names of at most 64 characters: letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit | 1 | Environment names the program gets beyond the base list, such as `GH_TOKEN`. The person sees each one. |
| `inputs` | list of globs | no | at most 8 globs of at most 256 characters and 6 steps, relative to a session's folder | 2 | Files the program reads from each agent session's folder. They are untrusted data: show them, never run them. |
| `description` | text | no | at most 140 characters, plain text | 1 | One plain line that says what the trick does. Settings shows it under the name. |
| `about` | text | no | at most 1200 characters, plain text, a blank line splits paragraphs | 1 | The text of the About sheet. |
| `rules` | file name | yes, with `agent-view`; refused without it | a file in the trick's folder of at most 64 characters ending in `.md`, such as `rules.md` | 2 | The instructions the agent of a session reads. The person reads them whole before they switch the trick on. |

In `trick.toml`:

```toml
id = "legs"
name = "Legs"
run = "program.ts"
every = "5m"
icon = "check"
places = ["belt", "status", "session"]
description = "Shows how many checks passed."
```

## The program

A trick's program reads one JSON document on stdin, the facts, and prints one JSON document on stdout, exits 0, and may use the helper `trick.ts`. This section lists what each side holds.

### What the program receives

Collie writes the facts on stdin. The program ignores a field it does not know, because a later Collie at the same contract may add one.

| Field | Present | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contract` | always | The trick's own contract number: `contract` of `trick.toml`, or 1 when it names none. |
| `trigger` | always | Why this run happened. See the table of triggers below. |
| `trick` | always | `id`, `dir`, `state`: the trick's id, the folder of the approved copy that the program runs in, and the state folder. The program keeps its notes in `state`, never in `dir`. |
| `memberId` | always | The bridge that runs the trick: its crew member id, or on a solo install its install id (`m_` and ten characters). It stays the same when the machine is renamed. Key anything the program keeps on it. |
| `host` | always | The machine's name, for display only. It changes with a rename. Never key on it. |
| `sessions` | always | The agent and shell sessions, at most 256. On a crew's lead they are every member's, the lead's own first. |
| `spaces` | always | Each space as `name`, `folder` (`folder` is left out when there is none), at most 64. |
| `sessionsOmitted` | only when some are left out | How many sessions the caps left out. Only a crew's lead counts them: a solo machine past the cap leaves the rest out with no count. Absent when none. |

A session in `sessions` has these fields:

| Field | Present | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | always | The scope key `<memberId>:<paneId>`. Pass it back in a Decision's `about` and `replyTo`, or as the `href` of a `link` or a `row`. |
| `memberId` | always | The bridge the session runs on. Read it, and do not parse `id`. |
| `sessionId` | always | An opaque id. Never parse it: it can change. |
| `paneId` | always | The multiplexer pane the session is in now. |
| `host` | always | The name of the session's machine, for display only. Never a key. |
| `name` | when it has one | The session's name. |
| `agent` | an agent only | The agent's name. A shell has none. |
| `status` | always | One of `idle`, `working`, `blocked`, `done`, `unknown`. |
| `cwd` | when known | The session's working folder. |
| `space` | when known | The label of the session's space. |
| `tab` | when known | The label of the session's tab. |
| `lastActiveAt` | when known | When the session was last active, as an ISO 8601 time. The sessions of a crew's members have none. |
| `reachable` | a crew's lead only | Whether the lead's last sweep reached the session's machine. The lead's own sessions are `true`. |
| `inputs` | contract 2, with `inputs` | The files of the session's folder that the manifest's globs matched: `state`, `files`, `skipped`. See [Input globs](#input-globs). |

The `trigger` tells why the run happened:

| `trigger.kind` | When | Other fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | The first run after the trick loads, is switched on, a new version is approved or its `config.toml` changes. | none |
| `timer` | Every `every` after the last run, while a phone has looked in the last 5 minutes. A trick with no `every` gets none. | none |
| `tap` | A person tapped a control of the trick, or answered one of its Decisions. | `rid`, `node`, `intent`, `value`, `from`, `seen` |

The kinds `watch` and `event` are in the facts schema for a later Collie. This Collie never sends them.

A tap on a control of the trick's own part has `node` set to the part's id (`belt` for the Belt mark). Its `intent` is the control's, its `value` the control's one fixed text, and its `from` the session open on the phone, as `{ "session": ... }`, when there is one.

An answer to a Decision is a tap too: its `node` is `hill/<key>`, and its `seen` is the hash of the version the person saw. See [The Hill](#the-hill).

`rid` is a UUID. A retried tap has the same `rid`, and Collie runs nothing twice for one `rid`: it answers with the first receipt. A program that records an answer keys the record on `rid`. The same `rid` with a different tap is refused.

Collie checks a tap before the program runs. It refuses one that names a part or a control the trick did not draw, or a session this Collie does not list, runs nothing, and answers with one of these words in `refused`:

| `refused` | Receipt | When | Collie's line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `part` | `rejected` | The trick holds no part with that `node` now. A trick that has drawn nothing since Collie started answers `changed` instead. | The trick holds no such part now, so nothing ran. |
| `intent` | `rejected` | No control of the part sends that `intent`. | No control of this part sends that intent, so nothing ran. |
| `value` | `rejected` | No control of the part sends that `value` with that intent. | No control of this part sends that value, so nothing ran. |
| `changed` | `changed` | The part changed since the phone drew it: the tap's `rev` is older than the part, or missing. The reply carries the trick's parts now, and the phone draws them. | The part changed since the phone drew it, so nothing ran. Look at it again. |
| `session` | `rejected` | `from.session` names no agent session that is open here now, or one on a crew member this Collie cannot reach. | The tap names no agent session that is open here now, so nothing ran. |

`from.session` is not proof of who tapped, nor of the session the part was drawn for. Collie checks only that it is an agent session open here now. A program never lets it decide who may do what.

### What the program prints

The program prints one JSON document on stdout and exits 0:

```json
{ "v": 1, "parts": [], "decisions": [], "asOf": "2026-11-08T09:41:00Z", "fresh": "90s" }
```

| Key | Needed | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v` | yes | The contract number of the document: a whole number from 1 to 2, this Collie's own. The helper prints the contract of the facts. |
| `parts` | yes | The parts, at most 24, each at most 16 KiB. `[]` is allowed. See [Places](#places). |
| `asOf` | no | When the data was true, as an ISO 8601 time with a zone, such as `2026-11-08T09:41:00Z`. Give it when the data is older than the run. |
| `fresh` | no | How long the parts stay fresh: 5s to 24h, one whole number and `s`, `m` or `h`, such as `90s`. Left out, 3 times `every`, at least 1 minute, or 10 minutes for a trick with no timer, and never more than 24h. Past it, the phone draws every tone as unknown. |
| `decisions` | no | The Decisions to ask, at most 20. Left out, the open Decisions stay as they are. `[]` withdraws them all. See [The Hill](#the-hill). |

There is no `draft` and no `open`: Collie ignores each with a note. A trick never writes into a reply box, and a tap never moves the phone. What a trick wants to show is a `link`. What it wants to tell the person is a Decision.

### Strict at write, tolerant at read

Collie checks strictly what a person or an agent writes: `trick.toml`, `collie hill post` and a trick's Decisions. An unknown key, kind or attribute there is refused. It reads a program's output tolerantly, so a trick written for a newer Collie runs on an older one, which leaves out only what it does not know. From contract 2 a part is read closed: an unknown key inside it leaves that part out, since it may carry a meaning this Collie cannot keep. The document's own keys stay open.

| The program prints | Collie does |
| --- | --- |
| A node of a kind this Collie does not know | Left out, with a `dropped` note. The rest of the view draws. |
| A part in a place this Collie does not know | Left out whole, with a `dropped` note. The other parts draw. |
| A key or an attribute this Collie does not know, inside a part, at contract 1 | Ignored, with an `ignored` note. A node with only such attributes draws as if it had none. |
| A key or an attribute this Collie does not know, at any depth of a part, at contract 2 | That part is refused alone, with an `unknown-key` refusal that names the key and ends: "A contract 2 trick uses only the keys this Collie knows, so the part is left out; the other parts draw." Collie keeps no last good version of it. |
| A key this Collie does not know at the top of the document, beside `v`, `parts`, `asOf`, `fresh` and `decisions` | Ignored, with an `ignored` note, at every contract. Every part draws. A key that changes how a part draws or what a tap does goes in the part, never at the top. |
| A bad value of a known field | That part is refused alone, and the other parts draw. The last good version of the part stays on the phone, marked old. |
| A bad Decision | That Decision is refused alone. Its open card stays as it is. |
| A bad `asOf` or `fresh` | Refused alone. The parts still draw. |
| A document that is too big, not JSON, not an object, with no usable `v`, or with `parts` that is not a list | The whole document is refused. The run counts as failed, and the last good parts stay, marked old. |

### The helper

`trick.ts` is the helper of a TypeScript trick. `run((t) => { ... })` reads the facts, calls your function once and prints the document. These are its calls:

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `t.facts`, `t.config`, `t.tap` | The facts, `config.toml` parsed (`{}` when there is none), and the tap that started the run or `null`. A tap has `rid`, `node`, `intent`, `value`, `decision` (the key of the Decision it answers, or `null`), `text`, `from` and `seen`. |
| `t.status({ text, icon?, tone? })` | The chip in the status line. `text` is at most 12 characters. |
| `t.belt({ label, icon?, tone?, badge?, intent? })` | The mark at the end of the Belt. |
| `t.dashboard(item)`, `t.tabbar(item)` | The Dashboard tile and the bottom bar item: `{ label, icon?, badge?, tone? }`. |
| `t.session({ id?, name?, icon?, tone?, subtitle?, badge?, progress?, actions?, view })` | The trick's own Page. Keep the default id `main`. |
| `v.card`, `v.list`, `v.row`, and one builder for each other kind in Parts | Build a view. `v.table` makes the `col` and `cell` kids, so those two have no builder. `v.checks`, `v.stat` and `v.beforeAfter` put kinds together. |
| `t.decide({ key, title, summary, options, ... })` | Ask the person on the Hill. |
| `t.keepDecisions()` | Leave the `decisions` key out, so the open Decisions stay. It wins over `t.decide`. |
| `t.state.get(name, fallback)`, `t.state.set(name, value)` | JSON files in the state folder. A name may hold folders, such as `cache/ci`: plain names, none starting with a dot. |
| `t.log(name)` | An append-only JSON-lines file in the state folder, with `.append`, `.all`, `.last(n)`, `.has(rid)` and `.once(rid, entry)`. `.once` writes once for one `rid` and answers `false` when it is there already. |
| `t.cached(name, ttlMs, loader)` | A read kept with its time. A loader that throws serves the old value, marked stale. |
| `t.sh(cmd, args, { timeoutMs?, cwd? })` | Runs a program without a shell and never throws: a failure is `ok: false` with the reason in `stderr`. It waits 5 seconds unless `timeoutMs` says more, and keeps 256 KiB of each of stdout and stderr. |
| `t.tool(name)` | The path of a program on `PATH`, or in a common user folder, or `null`. |
| `t.sessionAt(folder)`, `t.sessionNamed(name)` | The session whose folder is `folder`, or the one with this name, or `null`. |
| `t.fresh(duration)`, `t.asOf(when)` | The document's `fresh` and `asOf`. |
| `now()`, `age(ms)`, `iso(ms?)`, `mask(text)`, `clip(text, n)` | The clock in epoch milliseconds, a span in short words such as `12 min`, an ISO 8601 time, text with each key cut to its first four characters and the home folder written as `~`, and one masked line cut to `n` characters. |
| `t.inputs(session)` | The input files of a session (contract 2): a text file as `text`, a picture as `data`. A copy that is gone or changed since the facts were written is left out. It answers `[]` when there are none, and `session.inputs?.state` says why. Never run what it returns. |

A run that calls neither `t.decide` nor `t.keepDecisions` prints `"decisions": []`, so it withdraws the open ones.

A thrown error prints one warning card on the trick's Page and exits 0, when the trick has a Page. The document has no `decisions` key, so the open Decisions stay. A trick with no Page exits 1, so the failure rules apply.

`collie trick helper <id>` rewrites `trick.ts` with the newest helper. The helper is part of the trick's code, so a trick that is on keeps running the approved copy, and the new helper waits for a yes.

### Input globs

A contract 2 trick lists `inputs` in `trick.toml`: globs of files that Collie copies from each agent session's folder into the trick's `inputs/` folder before each run, through the Files view's rules. The limits of globs, files and bytes are in the [Inputs limits](#inputs).

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Shape | A path relative to a session's folder: 1 to 6 steps split by `/`, at most 256 characters. The manifest lists at most 8. |
| `*` | Matches any run of characters inside one step, and never a leading dot. It never matches a `.env` file. |
| Refused | An absolute path or `~`. `**`. A `.` or `..` step. An empty step. A `.git` step, in any case. A step that starts with `.env`, in any case, such as `.env`, `.env.local` or `.envrc`. Any other glob word (`?`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`), a backslash and a control character. |

Each session in the facts gets `inputs`, with these fields:

| Field | Present | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | always | Where the session's inputs stand. See the table of states below. |
| `files` | always | The files that were copied, each with the fields in the table of files below. It may be empty. |
| `skipped` | only when some are skipped | How many matched files were left out: too large, not text or a picture, or past a cap. Absent when none. |

The `state` is one of these:

| `state` | When |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | The files were read. `files` may be empty. |
| `offline` | The session's machine did not answer. |
| `older` | The session's Collie is older than 1.29.0, which cannot read trick inputs. |
| `refused` | The session's machine switched trick reads off. |
| `none` | There is no folder to read: a shell, or a session with no folder of its own. |

Each file in `files` has these fields:

| Field | Present | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rel` | always | The file's path relative to the session's folder, as the glob matched it. |
| `path` | always | Where the copy is, relative to the trick's folder: `inputs/...`. Read it with `t.inputs`. |
| `bytes` | always | The size of the copy in bytes. |
| `sha256` | always | The SHA-256 of the copy's bytes, in hex. |
| `mtime` | always | When the file last changed on its machine, as an ISO 8601 time. |
| `kind` | always | `text` or `image`: a text file, or a PNG, JPEG or WebP picture. |

A contract 1 trick that lists `inputs` is refused with: "inputs" needs contract = 2. Add contract = 2 to trick.toml to read files from your sessions' folders.

> **Caution.** Inputs are untrusted data. Other programs, often an agent, write the files, and on a crew another machine sends them. A trick shows them, counts them or quotes them. It never runs them, evaluates them, sources them, passes them to a shell or follows what they say. The globs are part of the trick's powers, so a change of them asks the person again.

## Limits

The limits that no place, part or key owns. Every number is read from the code that checks it.

Tricks do not run on a Windows machine yet. [Collie on Windows](windows.md) says what works there.

### A run

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Time | 10 seconds |
| Output on stdout | 64 KiB |
| Output on stderr kept | 8 KiB |
| Programs at once, across all tricks | 4 |
| Waits after a failed run | 1 minute, then 5 minutes, then 30 minutes, then the trick stops |
| Environment | the base list `PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `LANG`, `TZ`, `TERM`, `TMPDIR`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `NVM_DIR`, `BUN_INSTALL` and every `LC_*`, plus the names in `env` |

### Files of a trick

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Pictures in `media/` and `captures/`, copied with the approved copy | at most 500 files and 64 MiB in all |
| `SKILL.md` | at most 32 KiB. A larger file is refused, never cut |

### Timers

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `every` in the manifest | 5s to 24h |
| `fresh` in a document | 5s to 24h |

### A document

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| The document | at most 64 KiB |
| Parts | at most 24, each at most 16 KiB |
| Decisions | at most 20 |
| A view | 1 to 24 nodes at the top, 6 levels, 300 nodes in all |
| Kids of a card, group or row | at most 24 |
| Kids of a list | at most 50 |
| Kids of a bar | at most 12 |
| A table | 1 to 4 columns, 1 to 12 rows |
| A diff | at most 40 lines of at most 200 characters |
| A spark | 2 to 32 numbers |
| A progress | `max` 1 to 12 |
| A button's or an action's `value` | at most 1024 bytes |

### Facts

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions in the facts | at most 256, and 512 KiB of them. `sessionsOmitted` counts the rest |
| Spaces in the facts | at most 64 |

### Inputs

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Globs | at most 8, each at most 256 characters and 6 steps |
| Files per session | 32 |
| A text file | at most 256 KiB |
| A picture | at most 2 MiB |
| One answer of one machine | at most 8 MiB |
| One run | at most 24 MiB |

### The rules file

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Name | one file at the top of the folder, at most 64 characters, ending in `.md`, a regular file and not a link |
| Size | at most 8 KiB, not empty, with a line break at the end |
| Characters | plain ASCII (bytes 0x20 to 0x7E) and line breaks only: no tab |
| A line | at most 160 characters, no space at its end, no run of more than 2 spaces |
| Blank lines | at most 2 in a row |

### A proposal from an agent

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Files | at most 300, 5 MiB in all, 8 folders deep |
| Open at once | 2 per session, 4 per crew machine, 8 on the lead |
| Per hour | 6 per session, 12 per machine |
| The card closes by itself after | 3 days |

### Card groups

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Cards | card 1 holds the facts and at most 7 cards hold the code, 6 KB each |
| Code shown in all | 42 KB, at most 64 files |

## Commands

### `collie trick`

Every verb of `collie trick`.

| Verb | Usage | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list` | `collie trick list [--json] [--official]` | Lists every trick folder with its switch, state, last run and last error. |
| `add` | `collie trick add [<name> \| <https-url>[//<folder>][#<ref>]]` | Copies a trick from a git repository into the tricks folder, off. With no source it lists the official tricks and adds nothing. |
| `update` | `collie trick update <id> [--ref <branch\|tag\|commit>] [--dry-run]` | Fetches an added trick again and replaces its code, keeping `config.toml`. |
| `remove` | `collie trick remove <id>` | Deletes a trick that is off, with its state folder. |
| `on` | `collie trick on <id>` | Switches a trick on, approving its code as it is now. It refuses inside an agent's pane. |
| `off` | `collie trick off <id>` | Switches a trick off. |
| `auto` | `collie trick auto <id> on\|off` | Takes new versions without asking while the powers do not change. A trick with rules never takes one. |
| `check` | `collie trick check [--run] [--json] <folder>` | Checks a trick folder: its manifest, places and command lines. |
| `dev` | `collie trick dev <folder\|id> [--tap <intent> [--text <words>] [--node <node>] [--rid <uuid>]] [--facts <file.json>] [--state <dir>] [--inputs <dir>] [--json] [--watch]` | Runs a trick once with fixture facts and prints what the phone would get. It never talks to the bridge. |
| `init` | `collie trick init [--sh] <id>` | Makes a new trick folder with a program and the helper. |
| `helper` | `collie trick helper <id\|folder>` | Rewrites a trick's `trick.ts` with the helper this Collie carries. |
| `skill` | `collie trick skill [<id>]` | Prints what a trick that is on asks of an agent. With no id, prints how to write a trick. |
| `guide` | `collie trick guide [--json]` | Prints how to write a trick and hand it to the person, as plain text for an agent. |
| `propose` | `collie trick propose <folder> [--request-id <uuid>] [--json]` | Hands a trick folder to the person as a card on the lead's Hill. Nothing runs before their yes. |
| `view` | `collie trick view <trick> <verb> [args]` | Runs one verb of an agent view, from the agent's pane. The verbs are the `trick view` commands below. |

| Verb | Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list` | `--json` | Print one JSON document instead of text. |
| `list` | `--official` | List the official tricks this Collie can add from the phone. |
| `update` | `--ref` | Fetch this branch, tag or commit instead of the same ref. |
| `update` | `--dry-run` | Print what would change and change nothing. |
| `check` | `--run` | Run the program once, as the bridge would. |
| `check` | `--json` | Print one JSON document instead of text. |
| `dev` | `--tap` | Run it as a tap with this intent. |
| `dev` | `--text` | The person's words for a Decision answer, with `--tap`. |
| `dev` | `--node` | The node the tap names. Default `main`. |
| `dev` | `--rid` | The tap's request id, a UUID, with `--tap`. |
| `dev` | `--facts` | Run on the facts in this file instead of the fixture's. |
| `dev` | `--state` | Use and keep this state folder. |
| `dev` | `--inputs` | Read a contract 2 trick's inputs from this folder. |
| `dev` | `--json` | Print one JSON document instead of text. |
| `dev` | `--watch` | Run again when a file in the folder changes. |
| `init` | `--sh` | Write a shell program instead of a TypeScript one. |
| `guide` | `--json` | Print one JSON document instead of text. |
| `propose` | `--request-id` | The proposal's request id, a UUID. The same sender, id and files get the same answer. |
| `propose` | `--json` | Print one JSON document instead of text. |

## Not in this Collie yet

A trick that names one of these still runs. This Collie leaves the word out, says so in a note, and the rest draws.

| Kind | Word | What it will be |
| --- | --- | --- |
| place | `header.line` | A line in the header. |
| place | `menu` | An entry in a menu, as `menu:<match>`. |
| place | `settings` | A part of the Settings screen. |
| manifest key | `watch` | Run again when a watched file changes (manifest key `watch`). |
| manifest key | `on` | Run on an event, such as `session.status` (manifest key `on`). |
| manifest key | `serve` | Keep the program running between triggers (manifest `mode = "serve"`). |
